purpose: Describe a paused VM as portable inventory plus a restore/refusal plan before any cross-architecture whole-VM restore claim is made.

productIntent.problem: A VM contains mixed state: some portable, some target-native reconstructable, some unsafe across CPU architectures, and some unknown.
productIntent.goal: Pause a VM, inventory its contents, classify every row, restore what is safe, and refuse unsafe state with stable codes.
productIntent.notGoal: Do not claim exact arbitrary cross-architecture VM resume, raw vCPU replay, source ISA emulation, or metadata-only success.
productIntent.why: This makes mostly-whole-VM cross-architecture restore inspectable and honest instead of a vague any-VM promise.
productIntent.nextImplementationStep: Promote the retained real cross-arch filesystem, service, SQLite, and TCP-listener E2Es into machinen snapshot --portable and machinen restore consuming the Portable VM Manifest/Plan directly, with source and target architecture detected automatically.

workflow.name: snapshot VM
workflow.does: machinen snapshot --portable pauses/quiesces the source VM and detects the source architecture from the VM/inventory
workflow.why: avoid copying dirty or changing state

workflow.name: inventory VM
workflow.does: discover filesystems, services, processes, DBs, listeners, devices, and kernel state
workflow.why: know what is actually inside the VM

workflow.name: classify rows
workflow.does: mark each item portable, reconstructable, product-supported, refused, same-arch-only, or unknown
workflow.why: prevent hidden unsupported state from becoming a false success

workflow.name: plan restore
workflow.does: convert supported rows into target-native restore actions and refused rows into stable errors

workflow.name: restore target-native VM
workflow.does: machinen restore detects the target architecture from the target VM/host, boots target-native VM, materializes portable data, installs/recreates target-native services, and runs verifiers
workflow.why: cross architectures without raw CPU/vCPU replay

workflow.name: retain proof artifacts
workflow.does: keep manifest, plan, transcripts, refusal codes, and verifier output
workflow.why: public claims must be backed by artifacts

architectureDetection.source: machinen snapshot --portable reads the running source VM/inventory architecture
architectureDetection.target: machinen restore detects the target VM/host architecture before planning restore actions
architectureDetection.userSuppliedArchPolicy: normal VM workflow does not require --source-arch or --target-arch; overrides are for proof harnesses and refusal tests only

dispositionLegend.meaning: Can be copied or materialized without architecture-specific interpretation.
Can be recreated target-native from portable metadata.
A retained product path exists for this row and scope.
Known unsafe or unsupported; restore must stop with a stable refusal code.
May be restorable only without crossing CPU architecture.

validationRules: Every manifest item must have a disposition.
Every plan row with disposition=refused must have a stable refusalCode.
Every product-supported row must name a proofGate and artifactRequirements.
unknownStatePolicy=refuse-by-default must remain true for cross-architecture restore.
A manifest/plan alone must not raise a public arbitrary VM restore claim.
